extracted.intended_audience: researchers, institutions, and program managers seeking or administering Defense Health Program/DMRDP funding through CDMRP
extracted.subtask_description: Information and program-level standards describing the Defense Medical Research and Development Program (DMRDP) mission, scope, governance, and procedural expectations for applicants and administrators working with CDMRP on DHP research funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — life-cycle operational execution management
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide full life-cycle operational execution management for Defense Health Program core research program areas in support of advancing collaborative, innovative medical research and development to improve military community health and save lives on and off the battlefield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program's primary evaluative / operational objective is execution across the research lifecycle — from basic discovery through transition — with emphasis on collaboration, innovation, and impact on military community health and battlefield casualty care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations and program execution roles
rubrics_metrics.description: As directed by the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs [OASD(HA)], the Defense Health Agency, Research, Development, and Acquisition (DHA RDA) Directorate manages and executes the Defense Health Program (DHP) Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation (RDT&E) appropriation. The US Army Medical Research and Materiel Command (USAMRMC) Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) provides Defense Medical Research and Development Program (DMRDP) execution management support for the six DHP core research program areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and administrators should expect funding and program execution to flow through these designated offices and align proposals and budgets with DHA RDA / USAMRMC / CDMRP processes and authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic guidance and funding recommendations by Joint Program Committees (JPCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each major research program area is strategically guided by a committee called a Joint Program Committee (JPC), which consists of Department of Defense (DoD) and non-DoD medical and military technical experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JPCs translate policy and strategic guidance into research and development needs, make funding recommendations, and provide program management support; successful applications should address priorities articulated by the relevant JPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of execution agents for operational support
rubrics_metrics.description: Within USAMRMC, operational support for the JPCs is provided by multiple execution agents, including the CDMRP, individual laboratories, and advanced developers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program execution may involve partnerships or handoffs between CDMRP and laboratory/developer execution agents; proposals should consider operational pathways and partners for execution and transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research scope — emphasis on basic through translational research and product transition
rubrics_metrics.description: CDMRP provides program and award management support primarily for basic through translational research (Program Elements 6.1 through 6.3) and also works closely with the JPCs to transition products to advanced development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and program fit favor projects in basic, applied, and translational stages with clear plans or potential for transitioning technologies or interventions toward advanced development; applications focused solely outside these program elements may be out of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-tiered review and peer review participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The program employs a Two Tiered Review Process with programmatic panels and peer review participants (lists and panels are maintained, e.g., 'FY24 Peer Review Participants').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding decisions are informed by both scientific/technical peer review and programmatic review (panels/JPCs). Applicants should anticipate evaluation on scientific merit as well as program relevance and portfolio considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with programmatic focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: DMRDP funds research across specific focus areas (examples listed on the site include Traumatic Brain Injury and Psychological Health, Toxic Exposures, Spinal Cord Injury, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must align to one of the DHP core research program areas managed by DMRDP; applicants should select the program area that matches their research topic and address program-specific priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer involvement and reviewer requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The site includes consumer-oriented resources such as 'Consumers', 'Eligibility Checklist', 'Program Consumer Reviewer Requirements', and 'Consumer Experiences'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation processes incorporate consumer reviewers and consumer perspectives where applicable; applicants should consult consumer guidance and eligibility checklists and consider how their work addresses stakeholder/consumer relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding research duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: The site provides a resource titled 'Avoiding Research Duplication'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to demonstrate awareness of existing funded work and to justify novelty or added value, minimizing unnecessary duplication of prior research; proposals should clearly state how they differ from or build on existing efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement — follow application systems and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The site lists procedural resources including 'How To Apply' and 'Start Pre-Application (eBRAP)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow CDMRP/DMRDP application procedures (e.g., pre-application submission via eBRAP) and the program's stated instructions and timelines; failure to use required systems or follow guidance may render an application ineligible or noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program transparency — funding lists, programmatic panels, and participant records
rubrics_metrics.description: The site publishes items like 'Recent Applications Recommended for Funding List', 'Programmatic Panels', and 'Peer Review Participants'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and reviewers can consult published funding lists and panel participant information to understand prior awards, reviewer composition, and program priorities; this transparency can inform proposal design and expectations.
